name: hmm_regime_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Financial markets exhibit latent states (trending, mean-reverting, volatile-choppy) that are not directly observable but can be inferred from observable quantities (returns, volume, spread) using a Hidden Markov Model. By fitting a 3-state HMM on the previous session's 1-min data (observations: return, volume_ratio, range) and using the Viterbi algorithm to decode current state in real-time, we select the appropriate sub-strategy: trend-follow in state 1, mean-revert in state 2, and sit out in state 3 (choppy). The inefficiency exists because HMM implementation at 1-min frequency requires quantitative expertise and latency-sensitive computation. Most HMM applications in finance are at daily or lower frequency.
mechanism: Market microstructure varies across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes, mean-reversion dominates as market makers provide tight liquidity. In high-vol regimes, momentum persists as liquidity thins and stop-cascades amplify moves. Adapting the signal to the current regime captures the appropriate edge for prevailing conditions.

conditions: STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close < BB_lower
STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close > BB_upper

exit.signal_exit: HMM_State transitions to State 3 (choppy) — immediately flatten

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, require State_Prob > 0.80 for entry

weaknesses: HMM fitted on previous session's data assumes stationarity of state dynamics across sessions — this breaks down during earnings season, macro events, or regime changes
3-state HMM is a strong modeling assumption — true market dynamics may have more states or non-Gaussian emissions; model misspecification leads to incorrect state decoding
Forward algorithm computation at each 1-min bar adds latency (O(N²) per bar where N=3 states); with many stocks this may exceed latency budget for real-time trading
prior_art: Bulla et al. (2011) on HMM for stock returns; Hamilton (1989) regime-switching models; Rydén et al. (1998) stylized facts and HMMs; hmmlearn library in Python widely available but intraday application is rare
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
